reasons.realCost: Per-organization mass-email caps force the small-team bill onto Enterprise ($150/mo) and the growing-team bill onto Ultimate ($520/mo) purely to clear email-volume limits, roughly 2.5x and 3.25x what the same seat count costs on Standard.
reasons.pricingHonesty: Zoho publishes flat per-user prices for all five editions, including Ultimate, on its feature-comparison page with no hidden contact-count tiers.
reasons.smallTeamFit: Flat per-seat pricing and a genuine free tier for up to 3 users make it straightforward for a non-technical owner to start without an agency.
reasons.doesTheJob: It covers standard CRM and sales-automation functions but caps organization-wide mass email at 2,000/day even on its top edition and lists no native SMS feature.
reasons.freedomToLeave: Billing is pay-as-you-go with no contract, and users can switch between monthly and annual billing or plans at any time.
reasons.trackRecord: Zoho Corporation is a long-established, privately held software company, and Zoho CRM has been on the market for many years.

basis: Zoho CRM is a transparent, contract-free, and cheap entry-level CRM for a small business, but its per-organization mass-email caps mean the real monthly bill can jump two to three times the seat sticker price as soon as email volume grows, undercutting the predictability its flat per-seat pricing otherwise promises.
method: Two separate AI passes (two runs of Anthropic's Claude over the same evidence, neither seeing the other's score) scored six factors (1–5) and an overall; published overall is the mean of the two overall scores, rounded down. Pass scores: 3.3 and 3.8.
